doc.title: DeFranco Buddy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Content over commerciality
summary: He sometimes regrets not being commercial.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Little pause. Well, you have been accused of emphasizing content throughout your career over commerciality and do you ever have any regrets about following that path?

Sure, only because you know that if you deliberately gravitated toward the commercial part of anything that you do that you’re going to be more successful in terms of money. You want to get more money and you’re going to be able to get more things and all that stuff. So in that way sometimes I considered it’s unfair to my family to not be really commercial. But I feel also that if we get through and have a comfortable life, and Joyce has been great because she’s been able to help with our living to a great extent, so we are comfortable. But I regret many times that I can’t be like a lot of people who are gung ho for the commercial aspects in order to make it, to achieve stardom, or whatever that is.
And when you say you can’t be it just isn’t in your bones.
It’s not there, no, I’d be a big hypocrite. It just isn’t there.
